title: What a book or a person can give you
header_line: My analysis of one book on neuro-linguistic programming. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: Why should you spend your time on this person or this book?
A student said that many books claim to be one thing and then focus on a very small niche thesis that is not what you thought it would be.
I asked: why should I trust this person? Why should I invest my time exploring their ideas? What can this book do for me? What if I judge the book by its cover, and what do I miss out on?
I said I sincerely believe that when we meet a person we can develop a sense of presence: this person has a gift to offer me, and I do not want to assume it will be irrelevant in my life.
I said that identifying patterns also helps you decide whom you do not want to spend time with, because they carry negative patterns, which some people call energy or synergy.

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write a book or person you judged by the cover.
Write what it might have given you.
Write the questions you ask before you invest time.
Write a gift you were given by someone unexpected.
Write the pattern you notice in people you avoid.

check.q: What did I ask about judging a book by its cover?
choices: What do I miss out on

check.q: What did I say each person has?
What did a student say many books do?
choices: Claim one thing and focus on a niche

recap: Do not judge too fast. Look for what the person or the book can give you.
